text: Elijah stood on Mount Carmel with a nation watching.
The people had been pulled between Yahweh and Baal for too long. They kept trying to stand in the middle, but the middle wasn't faith.
Elijah called them to choose, and this day would make the truth plain.
Mount Carmel was full of people, noise, and waiting. The prophets of Baal had come in great number, and Elijah stood before them as the prophet of Yahweh. He looked alone, but he wasn't afraid.
The question was simple. If Yahweh was God, the people should follow Him. If Baal was god, they should follow Baal. The people didn't answer, and their silence told its own story.
Their hearts had drifted, and Elijah didn't flatter them. He didn't soften the matter or make peace with confusion.
He set the test before them so everyone could see. The God who answered by fire would be God.
Two altars would be prepared, one for Baal and one for Yahweh. The prophets would call on Baal, and Elijah would call on Yahweh.
No man would light the fire. That was the point.
The answer had to come from heaven, or not come at all. The people could watch, listen, and decide whom they would follow.
The prophets of Baal went first.
They prepared the sacrifice and called on Baal from morning until noon. Their voices rose over the mountain, urgent and loud, while the people watched and waited.
But the altar stayed cold.
The prophets kept calling, but nothing happened. They moved around the altar again and again, desperate for some sign that Baal could hear them. They shouted louder, but louder didn't make him real.
Elijah watched the whole scene. At noon, he spoke with sharp courage. Maybe Baal was busy. Maybe he'd gone aside. Maybe he was asleep and needed to be awakened.

The words cut because the silence had already told the truth. The prophets cried out even more and kept going until the day was nearly gone. Their bodies were worn out, their voices were tired, and their god had given them nothing.
Baal didn't answer.
The people had seen enough to understand what noise couldn't do.
A crowd can shout, and priests can perform with great energy. A false god can be served with passion, fear, and desperation. But passion can't make the dead hear.
The altar of Baal still had no flame. The mountain was waiting for the true God.
Then Elijah called the people near.
He repaired the broken altar of Yahweh, stone by stone, while the people watched. That mattered, because the altar had been broken like their faith had been broken.
Now it was being restored.
Elijah took twelve stones, one for each tribe of Israel. He wasn't inventing a new way. He was calling the people back to the God who'd already claimed them.
He prepared the sacrifice and laid it on the wood. Then he made the test harder. He told them to pour water over the sacrifice, over the wood, and over the altar.
They did it once. Then again. Then a third time. The water ran down and filled the trench around the altar, so no trick could explain what was coming.
No hidden spark could survive that much water. The people could see it with their own eyes. If fire came now, it would be God's fire.
Elijah stepped forward to pray.
He didn't shout like the prophets of Baal. He didn't dance around the altar or try to force heaven open. He simply spoke to Yahweh.
He asked God to answer so the people would know that Yahweh was God, and that He was turning their hearts back again.
The mountain grew still.
Then the fire of Yahweh fell.
It came from heaven and consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, the dust, and the water in the trench. Nothing was left untouched.
The answer wasn't small. God had spoken with fire.
The people fell on their faces. They couldn't stand in the middle anymore. Baal had not answered, and Yahweh had answered in front of them all.
They cried out that Yahweh was God. That was the truth Elijah had been calling them back to, not a new truth, not a hidden truth, but the old truth they'd abandoned.
The silence of Baal had shown one thing. The fire of Yahweh had shown another. The people had seen both, and now they knew.
The false prophets had been exposed. The living God had answered.
The mountain was no longer waiting.
The test was over, the fire had fallen, and the people had seen with their own eyes that Yahweh was God. Elijah had stood alone, but he hadn't truly been alone.
Yahweh had answered. The people knew.
The fire fell, and the lie broke.
